name: Food Allergies
overview: A food allergy happens when the immune system mistakes a harmless food — like peanuts, milk, eggs, or shellfish — for a threat and overreacts. Reactions range from an itchy mouth or hives to a severe, life-threatening reaction called anaphylaxis. There's no cure yet, so the main strategy is avoiding the trigger food and carrying epinephrine if your doctor recommends it. Most people manage food allergies well with a clear plan, careful label-reading, and the right medicines on hand.
symptoms: Tingling or itching in the mouth
Swelling of the lips, face, or throat

drugs.name: Cetirizine (Zyrtec) / Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
drugs.note: Calms mild reactions like itching and hives.

drugs.name: Epinephrine (EpiPen)
drugs.note: Lifesaving shot for severe reactions — use it and call 911.

drugs.name: Omalizumab (Xolair)
drugs.note: A shot that can soften reactions to accidental exposures.

drugs.name: Peanut oral immunotherapy (Palforzia)
drugs.note: Builds tolerance to peanut in tiny daily steps under a doctor's care.

redFlags: Trouble breathing, throat tightness, or widespread hives after eating means use epinephrine right away and call 911 — don't wait to see if it passes.

name: Anaphylaxis
overview: Anaphylaxis is a severe, whole-body allergic reaction that comes on fast — usually within minutes of exposure to a trigger like certain foods, insect stings, medicines, or latex. It can cause trouble breathing, a sudden drop in blood pressure, and fainting, so it is always a medical emergency. The good news: epinephrine works quickly when given right away, and most people recover fully. Anyone at risk should carry two epinephrine auto-injectors and know how to use them.
symptoms: Throat tightness or a hoarse voice
Dizziness or fainting from a drop in blood pressure
A sudden sense that something is very wrong

drugs.name: Epinephrine (EpiPen)
drugs.note: The first and most important treatment — use it immediately.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
drugs.note: Helps with hives and itching after epinephrine is given.

drugs.name: Albuterol
drugs.note: Eases wheezing once epinephrine is on board.

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.note: Sometimes given afterward to calm lingering inflammation.

redFlags: Anaphylaxis is always an emergency — use epinephrine immediately and call 911, even if symptoms seem to improve.

resources.label: Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America

name: Drug Allergies
prevalence: ~1 in 10 Americans report a drug allergy
overview: A drug allergy is when the immune system reacts to a medicine as if it were harmful, causing hives, itching, swelling, or — rarely — a severe reaction called anaphylaxis. Antibiotics like penicillin are the most common culprits. The key is knowing which medicine caused the reaction and telling every doctor and pharmacist about it. Interestingly, many people who think they're allergic to penicillin actually aren't, so allergy testing can sometimes safely open up more treatment options.
symptoms: Swelling of the face or throat

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
drugs.note: Relieves hives and itching from mild reactions.

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.note: For stronger or more widespread reactions.

drugs.name: Epinephrine (EpiPen)
drugs.note: For severe whole-body reactions — use it and call 911.

redFlags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a blistering, peeling rash after taking a medicine means use epinephrine if you have it and call 911 or get to the ER now.

resources.label: American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology

name: Insect Sting Allergy
overview: Most insect stings cause only temporary pain, redness, and swelling. But in people with an insect sting allergy, the immune system overreacts to venom from bees, wasps, hornets, yellow jackets, or fire ants — sometimes causing a dangerous whole-body reaction. Anyone who has had a serious reaction should carry epinephrine and see an allergist. Venom immunotherapy (allergy shots) can greatly lower the risk of future severe reactions, making time outdoors feel a lot safer.
symptoms: Large swelling that spreads beyond the sting site
Hives or itching far from the sting
Swelling of the face, lips, or throat

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
drugs.note: Eases itching and swelling from most stings.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone cream
drugs.note: Calms redness and itching at the sting site.

drugs.name: Epinephrine (EpiPen)
drugs.note: Lifesaving treatment for a severe allergic reaction.

drugs.name: Venom immunotherapy
drugs.note: Gradually retrains the immune system to tolerate insect venom.

redFlags: Hives all over, trouble breathing, throat swelling, or dizziness after a sting means use epinephrine if you have it and call 911.

resources.label: American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology
